quick.topic: Read the plan before you tune
quick.summary: Why adding an index did nothing, and three things to read in a query plan.
quick.takeaway: Find the costliest step in the plan. Fix that one.

parts.title: Read the plan before you tune

beats.line: My query takes four minutes. I added an index. Still four minutes. Why?

board.text: Read the plan before you tune

beats.line: You guessed the slow part. Ask the database instead.
Its query plan lists every step it takes. Read three things.
One. Which step costs the most.
Two. How many rows it expected, against how many it got.
Three. Any step reading a whole large table.
Skip most of it. Find the biggest number, start there.
The costliest step is a join reading far more rows than expected. Not the scan.
Now your fix lands where the time goes.

quiz.question: A query is slow. What should you do before changing anything?
options: Read the query plan to find the costliest step
Add an index on every column
quiz.explanation: The plan shows where the time actually goes, so the fix targets the real cause.

quiz.question: Adding an index always makes a slow query faster.
quiz.explanation: It only helps if the slow step can use it; the plan shows whether that is the case.
